resolution: The prima via itself defines moving as educing from potency to act (claim AQUINAS-ST-I-Q2-A3-REDUCED-BY-A-MOVER-A), and the case reads motus in that broad sense. Aristotle's physical change is one kind of such reduction, so the observation premise STMT-SOMETHING-IS-MOVED-IN-THIS-WORLD holds on either reading. All premises share `MovedIn`/`MovesIn` over an abstract `Respect`, so the formal results hold for any one reading applied throughout; an objection that the regress premises hold only for local motion is an objection to a premise, not an equivocation. Scope (#404): the typed Physics readings (TruthCore.Greek.Aristotle.Physics.Typed, docs/typed-physics.md) read `MovedIn`/`MovesIn` as physical motion. A universal prima via premise restricts to physical motion, so results that use prima via premises to derive typed Physics statements stay within one reading. The converse does not hold: Physics premises about physical motion do not extend to every reduction from potency to act. VIII.4's premises are therefore stated only for respects of physical motion (`IsPhysicalRespect`, DEF-PHYSICAL-RESPECT) and yield STMT-EVERY-PHYSICAL-MOTION-HAS-A-PER-SE-MOVER. They reach the root premise STMT-NOTHING-REDUCED-TO-ACT-EXCEPT-BY-A-MOVER only through the explicit, unattributed scope premise STMT-EVERY-REDUCTION-TO-ACT-IS-PHYSICAL-MOTION (result ARIST-PHYS-VIII-4-SCOPE-BRIDGE-TO-PRIMA-VIA), which is open and false on the broad reading if some reduction is not a physical motion.
